entities.name: Ellie Caulkins Opera House
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Ellie Caulkins Opera House in Denver, Colorado, opened in 2005 as the centerpiece of the Denver Performing Arts Complex (DPAC), is the home of Opera Colorado and one of the largest and most acoustically sophisticated opera houses in the American West. Named for Denver philanthropist Ellie Caulkins (who donated $5 million to its construction), it was renovated from the older Auditorium Theatre (1908) and features 2,200 seats with one of the largest stage footprints in American opera — enabling productions of comparable scale to the Metropolitan Opera.

The opera house's acoustic renovation, designed by Wrightson, Johnson, Haddon & Williams Inc. (WJHW), won international awards for solving the challenging acoustic problem of a horseshoe-shaped hall: the 2005 renovation introduced acoustic panels, ceiling reflectors, and a new 8,000-pipe Austin organ to transform a cinema-style auditorium into a European-quality opera house. The project is studied in acoustic engineering programs as an exemplary renovation.

Opera Colorado, founded in 1981, has used the Ellie Caulkins to present a full operatic season to Denver's growing cultural audience — a city whose altitude and dry air presented distinctive acoustic challenges that the renovation specifically addressed. The theater's location in the Denver Performing Arts Complex (the second-largest arts complex in North America) ensures year-round activity alongside the Colorado Symphony, Colorado Ballet, and Denver Center for the Performing Arts, making Denver one of the best-served mid-size American cities for performing arts.
